text: 86 real milestones from the last dinosaurs to the first humans now appear on the timeline at their real dates and fossil sites: the Wonderchicken, Titanoboa, the first penguins, bats, whales, cats and apes, Laetoli's footprints, heat spikes, a second asteroid off West Africa and more. Each card says what the fossils show and which study found it, and deep-time events now fly to where the place was on the drifting continents.

Smoother on phones: far-away trees, people and animals are no longer drawn when they would be smaller than a pixel, cutting the work per frame roughly in half. Mountains, ridges and valleys are now shaded so the terrain stands out, the biome colours blend instead of showing blocks, and rivers are brighter.

Every prehistoric animal checked against the Paleobiology Database: each now lives only near real fossil sites of about its age, and a few wrong dates are fixed (the cave lion and steppe bison no longer survive to today). 30 new real animals, from Ornithomimus and Austroraptor to Hesperocyon, the American mastodon and the straight-tusked elephant; 10 kinds of insects; and 17 real fossil plants, from dawn redwoods and nipa palms to southern beech, growing where their fossils were found.

Tour now glides from place to place every 20 seconds, never repeating nearby spots, with a card saying where you are and what lives there: tap Stay here to keep a spot or Next to move on. Crocodiles now live only on warm coasts and wetlands near real crocodile fossil sites. Tap any plant for its card. Fixed a panel peeking out under the buttons.

828 real volcanic eruptions and 817 historic tsunamis from NOAA's hazard databases, on their real dates and places: the deadliest erupt and send waves across the ocean, and earthquake cards now show how high their tsunami reached

The oceans now have their real depths: shallow shelves glow pale, the deep basins go dark and trenches like the Mariana are nearly black. Up close, the seafloor is shaped in 3D under see-through water, with ridges and trenches you can see.

The website now shares one world: everyone sees the same people and the same history. Now at humanitylivewatch.com. New first-visit walkthrough (replay it from the clock panel), a report button in chat, a 13+ check before posting, a privacy page, and a proper preview card when you share the link.

About 2,700 real significant earthquakes from 2150 BCE to today, from NOAA's global database: each strikes on its real date and place. The deadliest and biggest shake the globe; tap any for its toll, shaking, houses lost and whether it raised a tsunami.

138 real historic storms on their real dates: hurricanes, typhoons and cyclones with measured winds and pressures, plus record tornadoes, floods, blizzards, heatwaves, hailstorms and dust storms. Tap one for its record and toll.

74 more species die out on their real dates, from Haast's eagle and the elephant bird to the huia, Carolina parakeet, Bali tiger and Lonesome George, each marked where it was last seen. The endangered list grows by 50 with 2025–2026 IUCN status and counts.

69 more world wonders rise in their real years, from Göbekli Tepe and the Seven Wonders of the ancient world to Borobudur, Great Zimbabwe, Cahokia, Saint Basil’s, the Sagrada Família and Tokyo Skytree. Some fall, burn or become ruins on their real dates.
Earth reshapes itself on the real timeline: 115 landforms appear in the years they formed, from the Himalayas and Lake Baikal to Hawaiʻi's islands, Surtsey and the Salton Sea, with 71 new events

45 more historic journeys travel their real routes as they happen, from Hannibal's elephants over the Alps, Xuanzang, Mansa Musa and Ibn Battuta to Drake, Tasman, the First Fleet, Nellie Bly, the Fram, Shackleton, the Salt March, Kon-Tiki and Hōkūleʻa, plus the first car trip across the US and the first flights over the Atlantic, the Pacific and the North Pole

102 more prehistoric species from real fossil sites, from Albertosaurus and Rapetosaurus to Darwinius, Kelenken, the giant beaver and Smilodon, each in its real years and places; a live list of the prehistoric life alive right now in the Extinct panel

78 real historic earthquakes now strike in their real years with measured magnitudes and death tolls, from Messina 1908 to Sulawesi 2018, plus 38 more real volcanic eruptions from Kikai and Cerro Blanco to Novarupta and Hunga Tonga
Real recorded weather: from 1940 on, the weather panel shows the actual recorded weather for that day and place, and live weather once the sim reaches today

World wonders rise on the map in their real years and stay: the pyramids (gleaming white at first), the Great Wall, the Colosseum, Angkor Wat, the Taj Mahal, the Eiffel Tower, Mount Rushmore, the Twin Towers and more
Historic journeys you can watch on their real routes: Columbus, the Mayflower, Lewis and Clark, Magellan, Marco Polo, Darwin, Lindbergh and more
Real elevation and sea depth for the whole planet, real rivers and lakes, 16 biome types, giant trees like redwoods and baobabs
Famous landmarks get built in their real years, from Stonehenge to Mount Rushmore and the Burj Khalifa; the Grand Canyon carves itself
Follow a species and get an alert when it goes extinct; cloud on/off button; tap anywhere for a card about that spot
Ideas board with voting, live chat, viewer count, phone alerts, badges, clips, music and streamer mode
